branches.meaning: No latest read exists. Calls the original revalidate once.

The first revalidation condition holds; an existing read is dispatchCaptured, not dispatchNotified and not received. It is an observed state only: ambiguity/revocation may also exist, so do not label this automatically a usable queued snapshot or a bug. Calls revalidate.
Existing read began<=after and pendingDispatchAtOr0<=after, excluding the recorded branch2 subcase. Calls revalidate; may be an already complete older read, so do not infer in-flight.
began>after. Waits on the existing read.settled, possibly already resolved; no new read is necessarily dispatched.
began<=after but the notified actual pending-dispatch barrier is >after. Waits for settled or revoked; this is not yet completed coverage.
After the original await, current() is false. Returns without revalidation.
Pending hint revoked and another latest read exists. Continues the loop; this event is not a revalidate call.
Pending hint revoked and no distinct next read exists. Calls original revalidate.
Outcome failed; propagates the same original error. No error payload is recorded and no diagnostic retry is added.

Committed, effective began>after, original read.applied() true and original accepts(data) true; returns current data. A nonzero receivedProofBarrier is separately needed to identify an actual response-dispatch proof, rather than merely the conservative original fetcher-entry lower bound.
Committed, late enough and applied, but original accepts(data) returned false. Falls through; often followed by branch12 or13. Do not count this event itself as another read or retry.

No distinct next read after unsuccessful coverage. Calls revalidate. The reason can be discarded outcome, missing/old effective proof, stale cache identity, or a prior branch11 revision rejection; do not invent a unique reason without the corresponding events.
A distinct latest read now exists after unsuccessful coverage. Continues the original loop; extra is a read ID, never a began timestamp.

states.meaning: Connect begins after ++generation. Ticket/prepare can still be pending; this is not socket open or coverage.
Socket open. The subsequent event18 cause1 records the actual existing readBoundary for unconditional catch-up; open itself has no extra barrier field.
Validated live_ready was accepted and the original coverageAfter=readBoundary() assigned. This is a same-realm ordering barrier, not a wall-clock instant or snapshot revision.

closeSocket before clearing state. dispose/disconnected/visibility paths may already have incremented generation, so the close generation can be the successor of the opening generation; do not require exact open/close generation equality.
Existing acknowledged presence expiry updated coverageAfter. Distinct from socket ready; no new diagnostic barrier was introduced.

channel.subscriptionCaution: event17 first-subscribe is recorded before connect increments generation; subscriptions can survive later connection generations. Join by channelId+subscriptionId, not exact generation equality alone.

invalidation.note: pendingAfter is max of this obligation and an already pending one. The flush event19 after carries this value into readFresh. A max may combine more than one source obligation.

incoming.note: Recorded even when no key subscription currently matches; this can explain a later subscribe boundary beyond ready. Kind code0 means unlisted, not no push.

association.actualProof: event6 proofFunctionId→existing actualDispatchBarrier; event12 requestId→proofFunctionId; event13 requestId→actionId; event10 actionId→readId. event7 identifies the received proof barrier, and event2/F share cacheId+keyId. Never replace these links with nearest timestamps.
association.duplicates: Phase views are nondestructive. Identical prefixes may recur. Dedupe only identical tuples under the same launch/renderer realm nonce+timeOrigin+seq; a conflicting tuple is incomplete.
association.windows: authenticated-profile includes prepareNativeDevice after the original query window closed. Keep the old query window boundaries; do not attribute every exported event to login. Preserve pending reads at the stop boundary rather than awaiting them.
association.scope: These are local diagnostic integers. They never confer owner scope, authorization, snapshot status, SQL attribution for unknown contexts, or business acceptance.
